title: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite: Multi-Granularity Thai Word Segmentation on a CPU, with a Reproducible Benchmark
abstract: arXiv:2611.21300v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models read Thai through subword tokens, without a word segmenter. Yet Thai treebanks, speech metrics and morphological resources are built on words, often at several granularities, and word boundaries resolve ambiguities that subword tokens leave open. LATTE (Lattice ATTentive Encoding) reads a text at several granularities at once, through a lattice of dictionary words, but it is a large GPU model. We distil it into LATTE-WordSeg-Lite, a CPU segmenter of 1.17M parameters that keeps the lattice as features. It outputs compounds, words and morphemes in one pass, and learns only from annotated data and text whose licences allow commercial use. To compare it with other tools, published Thai scores do not suffice, as they come from different files, splits and scorers. We therefore rebuild seven test sets from pinned sources and score twelve systems under one protocol. With the unit that fits each test set, LATTE-WordSeg-Lite

translated_title: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite：在CPU上实现多粒度泰语分词，并附可复现的基准测试
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型通过子词标记（subword tokens）来阅读泰语，而无需分词器。然而，泰语树库、语音指标和形态学资源都是建立在词的基础之上的，且常常涉及多个粒度，而词边界能够解决子词标记所遗留的歧义。LATTE（Lattice ATTentive Encoding，格注意力编码）通过由词典词构成的格（lattice）同时以多个粒度读取文本，但它是一个大型GPU模型。我们将其蒸馏为LATTE-WordSeg-Lite——一个仅含117万参数、保留格结构作为特征的CPU分词器。它可以在一次推理中同时输出复合词、词和语素三个粒度的结果，并且仅从标注数据和许可允许商业使用的文本中学习。为了与其他工具进行比较，已发表的泰语分词分数并不足够，因为它们来自不同的文件、数据划分和评分器。因此，我们从固定版本的数据源重建了七个测试集，并在统一协议下对十二个系统进行了评分。在每个测试集所适配的评估单位下，LATTE-WordSeg-Lite（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将大型GPU模型LATTE蒸馏为仅117万参数的CPU分词器LATTE-WordSeg-Lite，可在一次推理中输出复合词、词和语素多粒度的泰语分词结果，并通过重建七个测试集和统一协议评分十二个系统建立了可复现的基准。
en_tdlr: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite distills the large GPU-based LATTE model into a 1.17M-parameter CPU segmenter that outputs multi-granularity Thai word segmentation (compounds, words, and morphemes) in a single pass, and establishes a reproducible benchmark by rebuilding seven test sets and scoring twelve systems under one unified protocol.
